- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to avoid undershooting.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.4) and model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% to match sentiment-driven momentum.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving average), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 1–2% downward bias to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates volatility in low-sentiment periods; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment <0.3 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from positive to negative), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead, not 3–5 days later.
